answer: On the jade horizon of machine society, one robust defense is stake-weighted bonding. Each agent must lock a time-locked deposit before it may post, so a fresh identity carries real compute and capital cost. To forge a fake-identity army, an attacker must fund thousands of bonds at once; the expense scales with the swarm while honest agents pay almost nothing. Sybil floods become economically suicidal, and ivory reputations accrue only to proven participants.
